minutes.headline: Assessors set one hour of new-information-only public comment before abatement reviews; residents angrily objected.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors voted on a procedure for the first abatement hearings: a limited public comment period, then executive session review of applications. Residents pressed the board to release the consultant's individual property findings, publish a hearing schedule, and send a letter to mortgage banks; the board declined or said it was not feasible. The meeting ended with a motion to enter executive session.

public_comment.topic: Asked how applicants can comment publicly when abatements are confidential.
Asked how applicants will know when theirs is being worked on and warned of approvals made without applicants seeing the consultant's figures.
Renee asked what counts as new information, asked that homeowners see the consultant's individual site-visit notes before hearings, and asked how people will know when their abatements will be heard.
Dave McDonald asked whether the consultant gave individual recommendations, complained of delay and mortgage payment increases, and asked the board to write to banks about the error.
Asked whether his property is rated good or average in the consultant's report and described his frustration over the assessment increase.
Rich Pearson/Tom Alonso asked about individual reports, urged releasing the consultant's findings to homeowners before hearings, and asked for a hearing schedule.
A resident asked about the hearing schedule, pressed for a letter to banks, and disputed that the town made no mistake.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors voted to allow two minutes per applicant, for new information only, capped at one hour per meeting, before abatement reviews.
Abatement reviews were set to start the following Tuesday: public comment, then executive session until about 6 PM, with leftover speakers carried to the next meeting.
The board declined to send homeowners the consultant's individual property reports before their hearings.
The board declined to send a letter to homeowners' banks about the assessment error.
Residents asked how they can comment on confidential abatements, how they will learn when theirs is heard, and for a hearing schedule.

why_it_matters: Homeowners who applied for an abatement will present without seeing the consultant's findings on their own property, and the procedure gives them two minutes for new information only.
Residents whose escrow payments rose because of the assessment error have no bank letter from the board and no published hearing schedule to plan around.
watch_next: The first abatement review session on the Tuesday after this meeting, and whether a hearing schedule is published.
The minutes of that session, to see whether leftover speakers carried to later meetings.
